"'''Common People'''" is the first episode in the seventh series of the British science fiction [[anthology series|anthology]] television series ''[[Black Mirror]]''. Written by [[Bisha K. Ali]] and series creator and showrunner [[Charlie Brooker]] and directed by [[Ally Pankiw]], it premiered on [[Netflix]] on 10 April 2025, with the rest of series seven.

The story centers around a woman ([[Rashida Jones]]) who needs a subscription service to survive, the consequences she experiences as the [[Enshittification|price goes up and the quality declines]], as well as the lengths her husband ([[Chris O'Dowd]]) is willing to go to in order to cover the cost of the service.

The episode received positive reviews from critics, with praise going towards the performances of the cast, the commentary and the ending.

==Plot==
Welder Mike Waters ([[Chris O'Dowd]]) and schoolteacher Amanda ([[Rashida Jones]]) have been married for three years and are trying to conceive a baby. One day while teaching, Amanda collapses, and doctors discover she has an inoperable brain tumour. Mike is introduced to Gaynor ([[Tracee Ellis Ross]]), a representative from tech startup Rivermind Technologies. Gaynor explains that Rivermind can remove the tumour and replace her excised brain tissue with synthetic tissue powered by their servers. While the surgery is free, Mike agrees to pay a monthly subscription fee of $300 to give Amanda a chance at living a normal life again.

Initially the service seems to help Amanda, but as time passes they find that it has several limitations (such as a limited geographical area in which it works) which can only be bypassed by upgrading from their current "Common" tier to the costlier "Plus" tier, which costs an additional $500 a month. Unbeknownst to Amanda, she begins interjecting brief advertisements into her daily speech. Mike secretly pays for the upgrade by raising funds on "Dum Dummies", a [[trash stream]]ing site where users take requests from viewers to perform humiliating tasks for payment. Mike initially performs these while wearing a mask to protect his identity, but reluctantly reveals his face briefly during a stunt to make a large sum of money. On their next anniversary, Mike buys a 12-hour "Lux" pass that allows users to access a new higher-level tier and manipulate their emotions and sensations via a connected app.

A co-worker discovers Mike's Dum Dummies livestreams and shares them at work. Mike attacks his colleague, who is then severely injured in an accident, leading to Mike being fired. Mike and Amanda plead with an unsympathetic Gaynor to be allowed extra time on Rivermind until Mike can get a new job. When Mike mentions that they are trying for a baby, Gaynor explains they would be charged an additional fee if Amanda were to become pregnant. Mike becomes furious and the couple dejectedly leave the office.

One year later, Amanda has returned to the Rivermind "Common" service, sleeping 16 hours a day and spouting ads when she is awake. Mike pays for 30 minutes of the premium Lux service, using it to boost Amanda's serenity, allowing her to calmly request that he end her life when she is "not here". After the time runs out, Mike suffocates Amanda when she blacks out to run an ad. Mike then walks into another room with Dum Dummies streaming live on his laptop, holding a box cutter in his hand.

==Production==
===Writing===
"Common People" was written by [[Bisha K. Ali]] alongside series creator [[Charlie Brooker]].<ref name=":0" /> Brooker originally conceived of the episode as a light, comedic episode that centered on someone needing a subscription service to remain alive. He got the idea from listening to a podcast in which the host broke from the story to deliver advertisements, then resumed telling the story.<ref name="TUDUM">{{cite web |last1=Hatchett |first1=Keisha |date=10 April 2025 |title=Let's Unpack That 'Perfectly Black Mirror Ending' to 'Common People' |url=https://www.netflix.com/tudum/articles/black-mirror-common-people-ending-explained |access-date=11 April 2025 |publisher=[[Tudum]] |archive-date=21 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250421215250/https://www.netflix.com/tudum/articles/black-mirror-common-people-ending-explained |url-status=live }}</ref>

"Common People" features several [[Easter egg (media)|references]] to previous ''Black Mirror'' episodes including, "[[Joan Is Awful]]" and "[[San Junipero]]". Additionally, it also references other season seven episodes "[[Bête Noire (Black Mirror)|Bête Noire]]" and "[[Hotel Reverie]]". The episode itself is referenced in "Bête Noire".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tallerico |first=Brian |date=2025-04-10 |title=Every Black Mirror Easter Egg in Season 7 |url=https://www.vulture.com/article/black-mirror-7-easter-eggs-episode-connections.html |access-date=2025-05-12 |website=[[Vulture (website)|Vulture]] |language=en}}</ref>

Brooker felt that the episode's ending was among the "bleakest" in ''Black Mirror''.<ref name="EW" /> [[Rashida Jones]] said she found the ending "mean" upon her first read, but came to understand its reasoning, finding it an act of love where providing a death with dignity is preferable to seeing the other person living in pain.<ref>{{cite web |author=Hibbs, James |date=11 April 2025 |title=Black Mirror's Rashida Jones reacts to Common People's "brutal" ending |url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/black-mirror-rashida-jones-brutal-exclusive-newsupdate/ |access-date=11 April 2025 |work=[[Radio Times]]}}</ref>

===Casting===
"Common People" stars Jones, [[Chris O'Dowd]], and [[Tracee Ellis Ross]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Puchko |first=Kristy |date=2025-04-10 |title='Black Mirror' fans, be warned: do not start with 'Common People' |url=https://mashable.com/article/black-mirror-season-7-common-people-warning |access-date=2025-05-12 |website=[[Mashable]] |language=en}}</ref> Ross and Jones were old friends and enjoyed working on the episode together.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Flook |first=Ray |date=2025-04-08 |title=Black Mirror Season 7 Star Tracee Ellis Ross Previews "Common People" |url=https://bleedingcool.com/tv/black-mirror-season-7-star-tracee-ellis-ross-previews-common-people/ |access-date=2025-05-12 |website=[[Bleeding Cool]] |language=en}}</ref> Ross and Jones both agreed to star in the episode before knowing anything about the storyline. Jones had previously co-written the season 3 episode "[[Nosedive (Black Mirror)|Nosedive]]".<ref name="DOG">{{cite web |last1=Mellor |first1=Louisa |date=10 April 2025 |title=Black Mirror: Rashida Jones Imagines An Even Bleaker "Common People" Ending |url=https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/black-mirror-season-7-common-people-ending-rashida-jones/ |access-date=11 April 2025 |publisher=[[Den of Geek]]}}</ref>

== Release ==
Ross spoke with comedian [[Seth Meyers]] on ''[[Late Night with Seth Meyers]]'' about the episode.<ref name=":1" />

=== Critical reception ===
The episode received generally positive reviews.<ref name="GR">{{Cite web |last=Sharma |first=Aayush |date=10 April 2025 |title=Black Mirror Season 7 Episode 1 'Common People' Review |url=https://gamerant.com/black-mirror-season-7-episode-1-review/ |access-date=10 April 2025 |website=[[Game Rant]] |archive-date=10 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250410122246/https://gamerant.com/black-mirror-season-7-episode-1-review/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="EW">{{Cite web |last=Nolfi |first=Joey |date=10 April 2025 |title=Black Mirror creator explains ending of 'Common People' episode starring Rashida Jones, Chris O'Dowd: 'Particularly chilling' |url=https://ew.com/black-mirror-common-people-ending-explained-11711717 |access-date=10 April 2025 |website=[[Entertainment Weekly]]}}</ref> {{Rotten Tomatoes prose|80|5.6|10|access-date=May 21, 2025}}<ref>{{Cite web |title=Black Mirror: Season 7 |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/black_mirror/s07 |access-date=2025-05-21 |website=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |language=en}}</ref> Louisa Mellor of ''[[Den of Geek]]'' rated the episode 3 out of 5 stars.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bojalad |first=Alec |date=10 April 2025 |title=Black Mirror Season 7 Episode 1 Review: Common People |url=https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/black-mirror-season-7-episode-1-review-common-people/ |access-date=13 April 2025 |website=[[Den of Geek]] |language=en-US |archive-date=11 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250411154914/https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/black-mirror-season-7-episode-1-review-common-people/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Proma Khosla of ''[[Mashable]]'' considered the episode the second most pessimistic of the show, behind only "[[The Waldo Moment]]", describing it as "a nightmare that seems terrifyingly possible" regarding capitalism using technology to make life worse.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://mashable.com/2018/01/05/black-mirror-pessimism-ranking-dread/|title=Every 'Black Mirror' episode ever, ranked by overall dread|date=5 January 2018|first=Proma|last=Khosla|work=[[Mashable]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210115161226/https://mashable.com/2018/01/05/black-mirror-pessimism-ranking-dread/|archive-date=15 January 2021|url-status=live|access-date=2 June 2021}}</ref>

''[[Vulture (website)|Vulture]]''{{‘}}s Ben Rosenstock disliked the episode, criticizing it as "jumbled on a tonal, narrative, and thematic level".<ref name="Vulture">{{Cite web |last=Rosenstock |first=Ben |date=10 April 2025 |title=Black Mirror Season-Premiere Recap: Life Stream |url=https://www.vulture.com/article/black-mirror-recap-season-7-episode-1-common-people.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250410082126/https://www.vulture.com/article/black-mirror-recap-season-7-episode-1-common-people.html |archive-date=10 April 2025 |access-date=10 April 2025 |website=[[Vulture (website)|Vulture]]}}</ref>

Netflix submitted Jones, O'Dowd, and Ross to be considered for the [[77th Primetime Emmy Awards]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=McNiece |first=Mia |date=2025-05-01 |title=Paul Giamatti, Chris O’Dowd, Rashida Jones, Cristin Milioti, Jimmi Simpson, and every ‘Black Mirror’ Emmy acting submission |url=https://www.goldderby.com/article/2025/black-mirror-emmy-acting-submissions-paul-giamatti-chris-odowd-rashida-jones-uss-callister/ |access-date=2025-05-12 |website=[[GoldDerby]] |language=en-US}}</ref> The episode received two Emmy nominations: one for Jones as [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie|Outstanding Lead Actress in a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie]], and one for Brooker and Ali for [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Writing for a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie|Outstanding Writing for a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie]].<ref>{{cite news | url = https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/emmys-nominations-2025-nominees-list-1236314909/ | title = Emmys 2025: List of Nominees | first1 = Hilary | last1 = Lewis | first2 = Kimberly | last2 = Nordyke | date = July 15, 2025 | accessdate = July 19, 2025 | work = [[The Hollywood Reporter]] }}</ref>

=== Episode rankings ===
"Common People" ranked average on critics' lists of the 34 instalments of ''Black Mirror'', from best to worst:
{{col-begin}}
{{col-2}}
* 8th – James Hibbs, ''[[Radio Times]]''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/best-black-mirror-episodes/|title=Black Mirror: All 34 episodes ranked from worst to best|work=[[Radio Times]]|last=Hibbs|first=James|date=15 April 2025|accessdate=27 May 2025}}</ref>
* 9th – Jackie Strause and James Hibberd, ''[[The Hollywood Reporter]]''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/lists/black-mirror-episodes-ranked/|title=‘Black Mirror’: Every Episode Ranked, Including Season 7|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|last1=Strause|first1=Jack|last2=Hibberd|first2=James|date=10 April 2025|accessdate=27 May 2025}}</ref>
* 12th – James Hibberd, Christian Holub, and Randall Colburn, ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ew.com/every-black-mirror-episode-ranked-11717539|title=Every Black Mirror episode ranked from worst to best|work=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|last1=Hibberd|first1=James|last2=Holub|first2=Christian|last3=Colburn|first3=Randall|date=18 April 2025|accessdate=27 May 2025}}</ref>
* 16th – Charles Bramesco, ''[[Vulture (magazine)|Vulture]]''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vulture.com/2016/10/every-black-mirror-episode-from-worst-to-best.html|title=Every Black Mirror Episode, Ranked|work=[[Vulture (magazine)|Vulture]]|last=Bramesco|first=Charles|date=10 April 2025|accessdate=27 May 2025}}</ref>
{{col-2}}
* 21st – Lucy Ford, Jack King and Brit Dawson, ''[[GQ]]''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gq-magazine.co.uk/article/black-mirror-episodes-ranked|title=All 34 Black Mirror episodes (including season 7), ranked|work=[[GQ]]|last1=Ford|first1=Lucy|last2=King|first2=Jack|last3=Dawson|first3=Brit|date=10 April 2025|accessdate=27 May 2025}}</ref>
* 28th – Ed Power, ''[[The Daily Telegraph]]''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/tv/0/black-mirror-best-episodes-worst-ranked/|title=Black Mirror: every episode, ranked from worst to best|work=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|last=Power|first=Ed|date=10 April 2025|accessdate=27 May 2025}}</ref>
{{col-end}}

''[[IndieWire]]'' listed the 33 episodes, excluding ''[[Black Mirror: Bandersnatch|Bandersnatch]]'', where "Common People" placed 21st.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.indiewire.com/features/best-of/best-black-mirror-episodes-worst-netflix-ranked-1201897973/|title=Every ‘Black Mirror’ Episode, Ranked (Including Season 7)|work=[[IndieWire]]|last1=Greene|first1=Steve|last2=Khosla|first2=Proma|date=12 April 2025|accessdate=27 May 2025}}</ref> ''[[Wired (magazine)|Wired]]'' rated it second-best of the six episodes in series seven.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wired.com/story/all-the-black-mirror-season-7-episodes-ranked/|title=All the Black Mirror Season 7 Episodes Ranked|work=[[Wired (magazine)|Wired]]|date=11 April 2025|accessdate=27 May 2025}}</ref> Instead of by quality, ''[[Mashable]]'' ranked the episodes by tone, concluding that "Common People" was the second-most pessimistic episode of the show.<ref name=":0"/>
